h1: The 8 Best Electric Kettles Under $200 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Electric Kettles Under $200: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best electric kettles under $200, from glass gooseneck models to 1500W stainless steel, compared on size and material.
summary: The Chefman with temperature control is the best electric kettle here, a 1.8L glass model with a gooseneck spout for tea and pour-over coffee at $25 to $50. The Cuisinart is the only $100 to $200 pick and matches cheaper kettles on wattage. The Amazon Basics steel kettle is the value choice.
intro: A $200 budget is far more than a kettle needs, and the spec sheets prove it: several kettles in this list cost under $25 and match the wattage of the priciest one. What extra money really buys is control, specifically temperature settings and a gooseneck spout, or simply a brand name. Boil speed depends on wattage and volume, not on price.

We reviewed eight kettles on paper, comparing capacity, wattage, material and any temperature or spout features. Because the ceiling is generous, the ranking rewards features over raw price. The list spans three price tiers, from under $25 to the single $100 to $200 model, and the cheapest steel kettle matches the dearest one on power, so the premium rarely buys speed.

products.name: Chefman Electric Kettle with Temperature Control
products.verdict: A glass gooseneck kettle with temperature control.
products.description:
This Chefman pairs a glass body with 1.8L capacity, a gooseneck spout and the temperature control named in the title, at $25 to $50. A gooseneck spout narrows the stream so you can pour in slow circles over coffee grounds, while temperature control lets you stop below boiling for green tea, which turns bitter in water at a full boil.

Those two features push it past the plain 1500W kettles below. It does not list wattage in our data, so you cannot confirm boil speed, which is a gap against the Amazon Basics steel kettle. Against the Cuisinart, it costs a bracket less and adds the features that the premium brand lacks.

Buy it if you brew tea or pour-over coffee. The caveat is the missing wattage figure, and glass needs gentler handling than steel.
products.idealFor: Tea drinkers and pour-over coffee fans.
products.skipIf: You only boil water for instant meals.

products.name: Cuisinart Electric Kettle
products.verdict: 1500W and 1.7L from a major appliance brand.
products.description:
The Cuisinart lists 1500W and 1.7L capacity, and it is the only pick in the $100 to $200 bracket. That makes it the one that uses the top of this budget, but the spec sheet shows nothing a $25 kettle lacks. It comes from a major appliance brand with wide service coverage.

It is second because the spec sheet shows no temperature setting or special spout, so you are paying for brand and capacity rather than new functions. The plain 1500W kettles below match its numbers for far less. It beats the Amazon Basics steel model only on name, as both list 1.7L and 1500W. Against the Chefman, it lacks every control feature.

Choose it if you value the Cuisinart name or want a retail warranty path. The caveat is price against equal specs, which is the largest gap in the group.
cons: Costs far more than equal specs
products.skipIf: You want the best value for the money.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Stainless Steel Kettle for Tea and Coffee
products.description:
Amazon Basics offers a stainless steel body with 1500W and 1.7L capacity, priced under $25. That is the same wattage and volume as the Cuisinart at a fraction of the cost. Steel is also the most durable material here, so it survives drops and does not show scratches as glass can.

It trails the Chefman because it lacks temperature control and a gooseneck, but if you just want fast boiling it is hard to beat on value. The Chefman plain glass model adds 0.1 L, though steel is tougher. The OVENTE steel kettle sits in the same tier with only 1100W, so this one boils faster.

Buy it for plain, quick boiling. The caveat is the lack of controls and a standard spout, so it is not suitable for slow pouring or tea at a set temperature.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants quick boiling on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You brew tea at specific temperatures.

products.name: Chefman Electric Kettle
products.description:
The plain Chefman combines a glass body, 1500W and a 1.8L capacity, at under $25. It is the largest kettle in the group by volume. Glass shows the water level and lets you see boiling, which some cooks prefer for knowing when to stop.

It sits below the Chefman with Temperature Control because it lacks the temperature settings and gooseneck, though it lists a confirmed 1500W that the control model does not. Against the Amazon Basics steel kettle, it adds 0.1 L and a see-through body but is more fragile.

Choose it if you boil for several people and like seeing the water. The caveat is that it has no extras, and glass needs gentle handling around hard knocks.

products.name: Cosori Electric Kettle
products.verdict: A plastic 1.7L kettle with no wattage listed.
products.description:
Cosori sells a plastic 1.7L kettle at $25 to $50, and the data we have lists no wattage. Plastic keeps the weight low, which helps when you carry a full kettle to the sink, and the 1.7L size fits a household.

With the Amazon Basics steel kettle offering a confirmed 1500W for less, the Cosori has to win on brand or looks. Plastic is light but the least premium material here, and a missing power figure makes boil speed a guess. It costs a bracket more than the steel model with fewer confirmed specs.

Buy it for a light, simple kettle. The caveat is the missing power figure, and check the listing for BPA-free wording if plastic contact with hot water concerns you.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a light kettle.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Kettle with Glass Carafe for Tea and Coffee
products.verdict: A 1L glass kettle with 1500W for tight counters.
products.description:
This Amazon Basics glass carafe kettle holds 1L and draws 1500W, at under $25. It is the compact glass option. A smaller body heats quickly because there is less water to bring up to temperature, so a single cup or two boils fast.

Only 1L means more refills than the 1.7L kettles, but the small body saves counter space. Against the plain Chefman, it gives up 0.8 L and keeps the same 1500W. It also costs the same tier. For one or two cups, the smaller volume wastes less energy than a big kettle.

Buy it for a single person or a small kitchen. The caveat is capacity: a group or a big pot of tea needs a second round.

products.name: OVENTE 1.7L Electric Kettle with 1100W Fast Boiling Water
products.description:
OVENTE offers a stainless steel body, 1.7L capacity and 1100W of power, at under $25. Steel wins on durability, and 1.7L is the same volume as the Cuisinart and Amazon Basics steel models.

The 1100W is 400W below the 1500W kettles, so it boils slower for the same volume. Amazon Basics steel is the better buy at the same price, which is why OVENTE ranks near the bottom. The wattage gap is the whole story, as everything else matches.

Buy it only if you find it at a discount or prefer the look. The caveat is the lower wattage, which adds to boil time on a full kettle.
products.idealFor: Buyers who don't mind waiting a bit longer.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1 Liter Electric Tea Kettle
products.verdict: A 1L tea kettle at the lowest price, with few specs listed.
products.description:
Hamilton Beach sells a 1 liter tea kettle at under $25. The only spec in the data is the capacity, with no wattage or material. It is a name-brand kettle at the lowest price, with a compact body for one or two cups.

That thin sheet is why it finishes last: you cannot compare its boil speed with the others. Against the 1L Amazon Basics glass model, which lists 1500W and glass, the Hamilton Beach tells you almost nothing. A shopper cannot weigh safety, speed or build from the data.

Buy it if you want a name-brand small kettle at the lowest price. The caveat is that you should verify the specs, especially wattage and material.
products.idealFor: One-person kitchens on a minimal budget.
products.skipIf: You want to compare power and material.

whatMatters.detail: Different teas need different water temperatures, and green tea is typically brewed below boiling. A kettle with temperature settings lets you stop at the right point, so the leaves do not turn bitter. Check the title or bullets for temperature control. Only the Chefman model with the control in its title lists it here, so check the setting range too.

A gooseneck has a long, thin spout that gives a slow, steady pour, which pour-over coffee needs to wet the grounds evenly. Standard spouts pour faster and less precisely, and tend to splash. Look for gooseneck in the listing. The Chefman with temperature control is the only model here that names one, so look at photos of the spout too.

Wattage sets boil speed, with 1500W faster than 1100W for the same volume. Some listings omit it, including the Cosori, the Hamilton Beach and the Chefman with temperature control. Look for the number in the specs, and compare it with the capacity, because a large kettle on low wattage takes noticeably longer to reach a boil.

Liters decide how many cups you boil at once. One liter suits one person, 1.7L to 1.8L suits a household. A bigger kettle boils more water than you need for a single mug, which wastes time and energy. Compare the listed liters to your usual use, and measure counter space and cabinet height.

Glass shows the water level and boiling, steel is tougher, and plastic is lightest. The material affects handling, durability and taste. Read the material in the title or bullets, since the Hamilton Beach does not list it. If you drop things often, choose steel, and avoid glass near hard counters.

faq.q: Do I need to spend near $200 on a kettle?
faq.a: No. Several kettles here cost under $25 and list 1500W of power. The extra money mostly buys brand or control features, like the Chefman's temperature settings and gooseneck.

Paying for the Cuisinart's price when equal wattage exists for less. The Amazon Basics steel kettle lists the same 1500W and 1.7L for under $25, so the premium buys only the name and a longer warranty path.

If you brew green tea or pour-over coffee, yes, because it avoids bitter cups. The Chefman with temperature control is the only one here with it. For plain boiling, it is not needed and just adds cost.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Rinse it, boil water once, and discard it before first use. Then fill it to the max line only. This clears manufacturing residue, and glass models like the Chefman should cool before you pour out the water to avoid shocking the glass.

Follow the manual's descaling method, and rinse twice afterward. A mild citric acid solution is a common choice. Regular descaling keeps the 1500W models like the Amazon Basics boiling quickly and prolongs the element life.

faq.q: Can I leave water in it?
faq.a: It is better to empty it after use to avoid mineral buildup. Leaving water standing leaves scale on the element and can affect taste, especially in hard water areas, and it speeds up wear.

finalTake: Buy the Chefman with temperature control if you brew tea or pour-over coffee. If you only boil water, the Amazon Basics steel kettle delivers 1500W and 1.7L for under $25. The Cuisinart is a brand decision rather than a performance one, and the Hamilton Beach needs its specs confirmed.
